details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml:180-182, 233-246, 275-278 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Telegram alert level is computed only from drift_results and error_results, so repairs of `match` results (created, updated or failed) leave the level at DEBUG, and the DEBUG body never lists repairs.
  WHY: The default ALERT_MSG_LEVEL is WARNING, so the DEBUG message is dropped and restore PRs or repair failures go unalerted. They show up only in the job summary.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:896-914 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Ownership of the restore branch `auto/restore-managed-workflows` is decided only from the tip commit's author email and subject, which are forgeable, before a force-push with GH_PAT.
  WHY: Anyone with push access can forge the metadata and get their branch overwritten. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT, and the others rated it MAJOR or gave no rating (the highest, MAJOR, is used). Minimax-m3 and glm-5_3-flash also note that the repo's own standard (a pusher-identity check) is not applied here.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:901-906 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The ownership check reads only the tip commit, so any later non-audit commit on the restore branch (update-branch merge, autofix commit) makes every later run return `restore_branch_not_owned`.
  WHY: The repair never refreshes that PR again, no alert is raised, and recovery needs a human to delete the branch.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:819-829 | severity=major | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `DriftRepairer._open_pulls` raises RepoFetchError when listing exceeds 10 pages (1000 open PRs).
  WHY: Repair fails for such repositories on every daily run. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT with confidence 2, and gemini-3_1-flash-lite rated it MAJOR with confidence 3.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:64 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The job-level gate skips the `update-wrappers` job in the source repository when allow_workflow_edits=false. README.md lines 132 and 1324-1330 say the opt-out is ignored everywhere and that `WORKFLOW_EDITS_OPT_OUT` is logged.
  WHY: This is a documentation mismatch. Only the agents.d/8065-managed-wrapper-integrity.md fragment documents the exception.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:847 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: DriftRepairer.repair catches all exceptions from `self._repair` without logging the repository name in the except block.
  WHY: Debugging is harder when several repositories fail.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:877 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: `if head_repo != repository: continue` is a case-sensitive comparison.
  WHY: A registry entry with non-canonical casing would never match an existing sync or restore PR, and the restore PR POST would fail with a duplicate-PR 422 reported as `repair_failed`.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:852 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `git clone --depth 1` runs for every drift and match result with no blob filter or sparse checkout, and `repair_drifted_repositories` (line 962) has no per-run budget.
  WHY: Slow clones, each capped at 300 s, could exhaust the job's 30-minute timeout and leave no summary or alert. Neither reviewer demonstrated an actual failure.
- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml:(git archive FETCH_HEAD step) and scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:load_renderer | severity=nit | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The audit executes the renderer module from the `stable` tree under GH_PAT without verifying the release attestation.
  WHY: This is a defense-in-depth gap only, since the tag is written only by this repository's release workflows.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Consumer repos can no longer change the managed workflow wrappers." (and the PR's "Branch ruleset" section)
  expected_change_site: A workflow or script that provisions the consumer branch ruleset requiring `coding-workflows/workflow-integrity` as a status
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The PR adds the status-posting integrity workflow but no ruleset provisioning, README.md:1331-1341 and agents.d/8065-managed-wrapper-integrity.md say the ruleset is applied manually by an operator, so wrappers are unprotected until then. Severity disagreement: gemini-3_1-flash-lite rated it BLOCKER, openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR, and sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT (a deliberate, documented rollout step).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:901-912 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Restore-branch ownership is decided only from the tip commit's author email and subject, which any repository writer can set.
  WHY: The audit could force-push over a branch that carries forged metadata. The risk is bounded because the branch name is reserved and the overwritten content is the audit's own restore content.
- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml:182 (related 234-246, 275-277) | severity=major | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The Telegram level ignores repairs of `match` results, so the level is DEBUG even when a restore PR was created or updated or a repair failed.
  WHY: DEBUG messages are dropped at the default WARNING threshold, and the repairs section sits inside the non-DEBUG branch, so these outcomes appear only in the job summary.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:_open_pulls | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A repository with 1,000 or more open PRs is reported as `repair_failed` because the 10-page cap raises instead of degrading.
  WHY: The failure surfaces as a per-repository error retried daily without success. This is only a theoretical boundary.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:901-906 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The ownership check reads only the tip commit, so a later non-audit commit makes every later daily run return `restore_branch_not_owned`.
  WHY: The PR is never refreshed again and no alert is raised, and the only recovery is deleting the branch by hand.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:877 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `if head_repo != repository: continue` is a case-sensitive comparison.
  WHY: A registry entry with non-canonical casing would not match an existing PR, and the restore PR POST would fail with a duplicate-PR 422 reported as `repair_failed`.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:852 | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `git clone --depth 1` runs with no blob filter or sparse checkout for every drift and match result.
  WHY: Only several consumers each near the 300 s cap would exceed the 30-minute job timeout, so this is unlikely.
- README.md and .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:64 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: README lines 132 and 1324 describe the opt-out as ignored everywhere, but the source repository's job is still skipped, with no `WORKFLOW_EDITS_OPT_OUT` line.
  WHY: This is a documentation mismatch, not a runtime failure, and the agents.d fragment already documents the exception.
- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml:(git archive FETCH_HEAD step) and scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:load_renderer | severity=nit | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The audit imports and runs code from the `stable` tag without verifying the release attestation.
  WHY: The trust boundary matches what the release pipeline already assumes, so this is a defense-in-depth gap only.
- TASK_GAP (severity=nit, confidence=2):
  Requirement: "Consumer repos can no longer change the managed workflow wrappers." and the PR's "Branch ruleset" section.
  Expected change site: A workflow or script that provisions the `coding-workflows managed wrappers` ruleset requiring `coding-workflows/workflow-integrity`.
  Evidence of absence: The PR adds the status-posting check but no ruleset provisioning. The README and agents.d fragment say it is applied by hand after the consumer has `ai-workflow-integrity.yml`, which is a deliberate, documented, operator-gated step.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: (1) audit_consumer_drift.yml line 182: compute `repairs = summary.get("repairs", [])` and include created, updated and error outcomes in the WARNING condition, and list repairs in the DEBUG body (about 4 lines). (2) audit_consumer_drift.py line 877: compare `head_repo.lower() != repository.lower()` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:901-912 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Restore-branch ownership is decided only by the tip commit's author email and subject, which are forgeable.
  WHY: An attacker with push access can forge them to bypass the `--force-with-lease` check and overwrite a legitimate restore branch.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:819-829 | severity=major | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: DriftRepairer._open_pulls raises RepoFetchError when PR listing exceeds 10 pages (1000 open PRs).
  WHY: Drift repair fails for repositories with more than 1000 open PRs even if a valid restore PR exists, leading to ignored drifts.
- scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:847 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: DriftRepairer.repair catches all exceptions from `self._repair` without logging the repository name in the except block.
  WHY: Debugging is harder when several repositories fail, because the failed repository is not identified in the log.
- TASK_GAP (severity=blocker, confidence=4):
  Requirement: "Consumer repos can no longer change the managed workflow wrappers."
  Expected change site: Provisioning of the `coding-workflows/workflow-integrity` required status in consumer repositories.
  Evidence of absence: The PR and agents.d/8065-managed-wrapper-integrity.md say the ruleset must be applied manually by the consumer repository admin, so wrappers are NOT protected in any consumer until a human performs a manual step that is not part of the automated sync.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py, `_repair` method: use a specific commit object reference or a signed commit to verify the branch tip (about 5 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/audit_consumer_drift.yml:180-182, 213-222, 233-246 | severity=major | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The Telegram level is derived only from drift and error results and never from `summary["repairs"]`, and the DEBUG body never mentions repairs, although `repair_drifted_repositories` (scripts/audit_consumer_drift.py:963) now also repairs `match` results.
  WHY: `tg_send_msg` drops DEBUG messages at the default WARNING threshold (scripts/tg_helpers.sh:86 and :113), so a failed or newly opened restore for such a consumer is invisible. README.md:1290 is not met for this case.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:64 (with steps at 87-91) | severity=nit | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The source-repository exception on the job-level gate skips the whole `update-wrappers` job when `allow_workflow_edits=false`, so the "Report ignored wrapper opt-out" step never runs.
  WHY: README.md:132 and 1324-1327 document that the opt-ou
